en: The *Buddhabhāṣita-kulikara-mahānāga-vijayā-tīrthika-vaśīkaraṇa-dhāraṇī-sūtra*.
Thus have I heard. At one time, the Buddha was staying in the great city of Rājagṛha. At that time, Ratnaketu...
The Bodhisattva Rāṇi addressed the Buddha, saying:
"For what cause and condition did the great nāga Kūlika swallow and drink a sharp sword?"
And as he was being surrounded by four-legged beasts,
the Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Ratnaketu-dhāraṇī, saying:
"In the past, in the city of Jñānavijaya, the Māra Īśvara of Akaniṣṭha..."
When the Vidyārāja Acala engaged in debate with the non-Buddhists,
he together produced various supernatural transformations to manifest wisdom.
At that time, the Vidyārāja Acala transformed into a sword of the fire of wisdom.
At that time, there were ninety-five kinds of non-Buddhist practitioners (tīrthika).
Their leader was named Jñānaprabha,
who had also perfected the "Wisdom-Fire Sword."
Then, the Great Sword of the Wisdom-Fire of the Immovable Wisdom King (Acala) transformed into the great four-limbed dragon Kuliśvara,
who is the embodiment of the four Great Vidyārājas: Trailokyavijaya, Mahābala, Yamāntaka, and Takkirāja-Vajrayakṣa.
King Grīvā possesses a lotus named Jñānāgnigarbha, adorned with the syllable Kūlika,
which is one hundred thousand yojanas in height.
From its mouth, it emits a breath like twenty trillion peals of thunder sounding simultaneously.
Having heard this, the non-Buddhists, Māras, and others abandoned their evil doubts and heterodox attachments.
The Buddha spoke this dhāraṇī:
*Namo siddhi siddhi susiddhi-garāya kūryaṃ samasamasi artha-siddhi svāhā.* By the power of this mantra, all inauspiciousness is eliminated and all Māra kings are subdued.
If someone is afflicted by a malevolent spirit,
write down their name and recite this mantra twenty-one times.
In an instant, the malevolent spirits were suddenly consumed by flames.
One must sever the consumption of the five pungent roots, alcohol, and meat,
and refrain from being defiled by women or impure attachments.
If one recites this mantra with single-minded devotion,
all that is sought shall certainly be fulfilled.
It causes trees to bloom out of season.
The four oceans become mountains, and Mount Sumeru, the King of Mountains, becomes an ocean.
This is the majestic power of this mantra, the merit of this mantra.
Burning ice is like oil; the *Avaṅkṣa* tree is like water.
Everything follows the mind,
just like Baka Brahmā. Therefore,
he spoke this verse again:
The practitioner of service, like Bhagavan who has attained samādhi,
shares the same station as the Bodhisattva;
one should recite the name of the Kulika Dragon.
The Buddha spoke this sutra to eliminate demonic obstacles in the present life and to ensure rebirth in the Land of Peace and Bliss hereafter.
All the evil Mara kings and the ninety-five kinds of great dragon kings [were present].
With great joy, they received it with faith and practiced accordingly.
The *Kulika-rāja-nāga-dhāraṇī-sūtra* is hereby concluded.
